text:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx on streaming gateway and increased client disconnects for paged/stream endpoints. Affected regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1. Error rate: 4.5% -> 12% over last 10m. Seen as 502/504 and a lot of connection resets. Paging fanout traces show partial responses followed by resets. Dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/streaming-errors

sam_oncall: seeing lots of 502s from gateway -> upstream reset. Clients report partial outputs + sudden stop. Paging rate also spiking. I'm paging eng-runtime + SRE. tagging @lina_runtime @matt_sre

lina_runtime: joining. grabbing perf traces and tailing runtime logs. Early thought: KV cache hotpath might be thrashing under bursty fanout leading to longer latencies and upstream timeouts. Also seeing some 499s (client cancels) at the gateway level which complicates metrics.

matt_sre: I can confirm increased RSTs from NLB in front of gateway around 10:01:30Z. Kernel tcp retransmits climbing on gateway instances. Rolling back a recent NLB target-group healthcheck change is an option. I'm also checking whether there's a gradual CPU steal on the node group.

ana_support: FYI CS is getting 3 tickets from a single customer (acme-inc) complaining that streaming sessions cut out mid-response. They've attached cURL logs showing connection closed after a few chunks.

lina_runtime: pasting a snippet from the runtime logs showing chunked encoding close events:

```
2026-03-15T10:01:27Z INFO stream_id=wu-23 chunk_sent bytes=1536
2026-03-15T10:01:28Z WARN stream_id=wu-23 upstream_reset reason=RST_STREAM code=0
2026-03-15T10:01:28Z ERROR stream_id=wu-23 handler=stream_writer client_cancelled=true
```

lina_runtime: also seeing an uptick in request wall-time for paged requests (tailing at ~12s) before the reset. Looks correlated with a burst of heavy prompt lengths from a specific API key set.

sam_oncall: actionable items: 1) Can SRE check NLB target health and revert last change? 2) Runtime team to enable non-streaming fallback for high error-rate customers or temporarily pin to paged endpoints? 3) Support to inform affected customers with a short blurb.

matt_sre: rolling back NLB healthcheck change now (started). If that drops resets we can consider this mitigated. ETA ~3m.

[deploy-bot]: `revert-target-group-healthcheck 2026-03-15T09:58:00Z by infra-ops` initiated by matt_sre

matt_sre: Revert completed. Monitoring...

lina_runtime: while we watch the NLB, I can flip a runtime flag to switch heavy fanout paged requests to a conservative batching mode that reduces concurrency per backend. Doing a quick config change: `STREAM_BATCH_POLICY=conservative` on the runtime fleet for high-latency routes. Applying to canary first.

lina_runtime: canary applied to 10% of runtime fleet. Observability note: enabling more backpressure on the worker pool to avoid KV cache thrash.

sam_oncall: support blurb draft -> "We're investigating increased disconnections on streaming endpoints and may route some traffic to paged fallbacks while we stabilize. We're prioritizing impacted customers. We'll update in 30m or on resolution." Approve? @jin_product

jin_product: approve, add "no data loss expected; partial responses may have been delivered." Keep it succinct.

ana_support: sent to affected customers (acme-inc, beta-corp).

matt_sre: NLB rollback reduced RSTs by ~70% in 1m. 5xx rate dropped from 12% to 6% so far. Kernel retransmits have normalized on a subset of instances.

lina_runtime: canary with conservative batching shows decreased tail latencies on those nodes: paged request P95 down from 11.8s to 4.2s. Streaming client cancels reduced on canary routes. Will scale rollout to 50% if numbers hold.

sam_oncall: scaling the conservative batch policy to 50% now. Leaving 50% default so we can compare.

lina_runtime: rolling to 50% done. Telemetry: error rate continues to drop, streaming disconnects are down ~60% cluster-wide.

matt_sre: I'll keep the NLB change rolled back and open a ticket with infra to audit the target-group settings. Looks like the earlier tweak shortened the grace period and caused premature connection terminations under transient backend slowness.

lina_runtime: follow-up: root cause hypothesis = combination of (1) NLB healthcheck/conn settings causing RSTs on transient backend slowness + (2) runtime KV/cache hotpath thrash under bursty fanout; mitigation = NLB rollback + conservative backpressure/batching. Next steps: deeper trace collection and a small perf patch to KV eviction algorithm.

matt_sre: opening incident ticket and tagging infra team (infra-ops). Will also schedule a maintenance window to test healthcheck variations in staging.

sam_oncall: status update to #general in 15m. Preparing postmortem skeleton.

ana_support: any customer impacts to surface in a status page? severity?
sam_oncall: yes, set as partial-degradation for streaming endpoints in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for ~35m window. Note mitigations and customer guidance.

jin_product: request for product: prepare a short FAQ for customers about streaming fallbacks and how to opt into paged endpoints if they prefer reliability over streaming.

lina_runtime: sketch of diagnostic commands for Eng/SRE to reproduce from a test client:

```
# reproduce streaming partial chunks
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -X POST https://streaming-api.redwood/v1/generate \
  -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>","stream":true}'

# tcpdump on gateway to capture resets
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <client-ip> and tcp and port 443 -w /tmp/stream-resets.pcap
```

matt_sre: attaching kernel netstat snippet showing TIME_WAIT/RST spike:

```
# netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
12456
# ss -s
TCP:   15418 (estab 1024, closed 12345, orphaned 0, synrecv 0, timewait 12456)
```

sam_oncall: current status: mitigations applied (NLB rollback + runtime conservative batching), error rates decreasing but not fully back to baseline. Keeping this thread open until fully stable and PM/infra postmortem items created.

lina_runtime: assigning follow-ups:
- runtime: KV eviction perf patch (PR in progress) -> owner: lina_runtime
- infra: audit NLB healthcheck change + staging test -> owner: matt_sre/infra-ops
- support: customer communications and status page -> owner: ana_support
- product: FAQ & opt-in guidance -> owner: jin_product

matt_sre: tagging oncall followup: @sam_oncall -> please coordinate postmortem and severity classification.

sam_oncall: noted. I'll triage the postmortem and attach logs/traces. Handoff to next on-call in 30m if still open.

ana_support: thanks everyone — keeping customers updated.

[One hour later]

sam_oncall: handing off still-open incident to @eve_oncall for further follow-up and postmortem write-up. Current status: error rate stabilized at ~1.2% (close to baseline). KV patch in review. Infra to verify NLB rollout plan.

eve_oncall: acknowledged, taking over.
